To expedite consideration of matters covered by the Annual Commu
nication, the President assigned to the Committee on Unflnished Business
the question of Song Books, and to the Committee on New Business the

questions of Fraternity Alumni Associations and General Fraternity
Secretary.
Bro. Parks {Lambda) offered the following resolution :

Resolved, That Section 6 of Article II. of the Constitution be
amended so as to read as follows :
Section 6. The convention held in the year 1908 shall [an
nually] elect an Executive Council of [five] nine, a majority of
whom shall be graduate members of the Fraternity and no more
than two from the same Chapter. The said Council, at its fl,rst

meeting after its election, shall divide itself by lot into three
classes of three members each, whose respective terms of office
shall be one, two and three years. Thereafter, the Convention
shall annually elect three members to replace the outgoing class
and to serve three years each. A member of the Council, at the
expiration of a full term of three years, shall not be eligible for
re-election to the Council at the Convention at which his term
expires. The headquarters of [this] the Council shall be in the
City of New York. The Council shall elect a President, a Secre
tary and Treasurer, shall regulate its own proceedings and assign
ments of duty and shall be empowered to employ a member of

G

the Fraternity to act as Assistant Secretary, who shall receive
therefor such compensation as shall be authorized by the Conven
tion. [This] The Council shall issue calls and make all arrange
ments lor special Conventions, when requested so to do, ,in
writing, by at least five Chapters; shall give facial announce
ment of the passage of any measure requiring the consent of the
Chapters ; shall keep the Fraternity seal, all Fraternity property,
the official copy ot the Constitution and Convention records, a
copy of the laws of each Chapter and as complete statistics of
them as possible. It shall have power under the regulation of
the Convention to make and collect assessments of the several
Chapters in proportion to the number of members in each ; shall
a'low claims against the Fraternity ; shall superintend the publi
cation of Fraternity documents ; and shall decide all points at
issue between Chapters when appealed to. The [Executive]
Council shall fill its own vacancies and shall submit annually to
the Convention a communication embracing a report of [their] its
transactions with such recommendations as to the affairs of the

Fraternity as [they] it may deem proper. The Council may inves
tigate applications for charters of the Fraternity and, upon its
own motion, may inquire into the expediency of establishing a

Chapter at any college or university. Within thirty days after
the close of any such investigation or inquiry, the Council shall
transmit to each Chapter or to the Convention its findings of fact
and recommendation. The Council shall, at regular periods, cause
the Chapters to be visited by one or more of its members, the ex
pense of such visitation to be met out of funds to be specially con
tributed 01- otherwise provided for that purpose. The contents of
any report on such visitation shall be communicated only to the
Council and to the members or alumni of the Chapter visited.

Note : The matter in italic is new matter.

The matter in brackets [ ] is old matter to be omitted.

The resolution was referred to the Committee on New Business.

7

The President announced that the Convention photograph would be
taken at 12 o'clock in front of the Chapter House.

Recess until 2 P. M.

Meeting called to order at 3 P. M., President Bridgman in the Chair.
Bro. George Welling Giddings (Lambda '92), Treasurer of the Council.
addressed the meeting, stating that an unused balance in the Founders'
Fund made it possible to place bronze memorial tablets of the Founders
in the several chapter houses.*

Bro. Edwin Louis Garvin {Delta '97), presented an altar to the Delta
Chapter as an anniversary gift of the 1897 delegation. It was the handi
work of Bro. Erik Wilhelm Wallin {Delta 97), and was designed by Bro.
Arthur Durant Sneden {Delta '96). Bro. Payson a'ckaowledged the gift
on behalf of the Chapter.

The President called for the report of the Committee to nominate an

Executive Council. Report not ready.
The Committee on Unflnished Business reported three resolutions :

1. In relation to the Fraternity Song Books. Adopted. {General
Resolution No. 1.)

2. In relation to the establishment of the office of General Fraternity
Secretary.
This resolution was laid on the table.

3. In relation to the Alumni Associations.

This resolution was laid on the table.

Motion was carried to take from the table for discussion the resolu
tion reported by the Committee on Unfinished Business in relation to
establishing the office of General Fraternity Secretary. The resolution
submitted to the Committee, and which it reported adversely, was as
follows :

"resolutions.

Whereas, it appears that our undergraduates have to a considerable
extent lost touch with the central body, with chapters other than their
own, and even in some cases with their local alumni, and

9

Whereas, it seems desirable to us that this condition should be cor
rected as soon as may be, and that it could be substantially remedied by
the establishment of closer relations between the council and the chap
ters, now it is
Resolved by the General Convention of the Psi Upsilon Frater
nity That the Executive Council be requested to resume visit

ation of the several Chapters at such frequent intervals as may
be found possible ; and that the Council be authorized and re
quested to employ, from among the members of the Fraternity,
for its assistance in accomplishing this end, a person or persons
whose compensation shall be supplied out of such funds as may
be raised by subscription within the alumni body of this
Fraternity."

After a very full discussion, in which many of the brethren partici
pated, the resolution was lost by the following vote : Ayes Theta, 

Delta, Sigma, Xi, Phi, Pi, Beta Beta, Rho, Omega, 9.

Noes Beta, Gamma, Zeta, Lambda, Kappa, Psi, Upsilon, Iota, Chi,

Eta, Tau, Mu, Upsilon, Second, Third, Fourth and Fifth Graduates, 17.

As to Masters of the Rolls {General Resolution No. 6).

RESOLUTIONS ADOPTED.
general resolutions.

General Resolution No. 1 Resolved, that the Convention hereby
authorizes the publication of. five hundred copies of the revised Song
Book, to be sold for two dollars each, and that in accordance with the
provision made by the Convention of 1892, Brother Karl P. Harrington
{Xi '82), be paid a royalty of forty cents upon each Song Book sold of the
new edition.

General Resolution No. 2 Resolved, That Section 6 of Article II. of
the Constitution be amended so as to read as follows :

Section 6. The Convention held in the year 1908 shall elect an
Executive Council of ten, a majority of whom shall be graduate members
of the Fraternity and no more than two from the same Chapter. The
said Council, at its flrst meeting after its election, shall divide itself
by lot
into Ave classes of two members each, whose respective terms of office
shall be one, two, three, four and five years. Thereafter, the Convention
shall annually elect two members to replace the outgoing class and to
serve five years each. The headquarters of the Council shall be in the
City of New York. The Council shall elect a President, a Secretary and
Treasurer, shall regulate its own proceedings and assignments of duty
and shall be empowered to employ a member of the Fraternity to act as
Assistant Secretary, and who shall receive therefor such compensation as
shall be authorized by the Convention. The Council shall issue calls and
make all arrangements for special Conventions, when
requested so to do,
in writing, by at least five Chapters ; shall give official announcement of
the passage of any measure requiring the consent of the
Chapters ; shall

11

keep the Fraternity seal, all Fraternity property, the official copy of the
Constitution and Convention records, a copy of the laws of each Chapter
and as complete statistics of them as possible. It shall have power
under the regulation of the Convention to make and collect assessments
on the several Chapters in proportion to the number of members in each;

shall allow claims against the Fraternity ; shall superintend the publica
tion of Fraternity documents ; and shall decide all points at issue between
Chapters when appealed to. The Council shall fill its own vacancies and
shall submit annually to the Convention a communication embracing a
report of its transactions with such recommendations as to the affairs of
the Fraternity as it may deem proper. The Council may investigate

applications for charters of the Fraternity and, upon its own motion, may
inquire into the expediency of establishing a Chapter at any college or
university. Within thirty days after the close of any such investigation or
inquiry, the Council shall transmit to each Chapter or to the Convention
its findings of fact and recommendation. The Council shall, at regular
periods, cause the Chapters to be visited by one or more of its members,
the expense of such visitation to be met out of funds to be specially con
tributed or otherwise provided for that purpose. The contents of any

report on such visitation shall be communicated only to the Council and
to the members or alumni of the Chapter visited.

General Resolution No. 3 Resolved, That the Executive Council is

hereby authorized to ascertain the particulars of existing Alumni Associa
tions of the Fraternity and to follow out the ideas suggested in paragraph
V of the Annual Communication of the Council to the Convention of 1907.

General Resolution No. 4 

Resolved, That the matter of granting a
Chapter of the Fraternity to the Aztec Club of the University of Illinois
be referred to the Chapters before the next Convention.
General Resolution No. 5 Whereas, The following Resolution pre

pared by Bro. Charles S. F. Lincoln {Kappa '91) has been submitted to
the Convention :

"Resolved, That a Bulletin of the Fraternity be published,
either annually or semi-annually, for distribution among the
Alumni, containing the list of initiates, deaths, expulsions, and
such other personal information or other matter of Fraternity
interest the Council may consider advisable to publish; this
as

Bulletin to be printed and distributed for one year on trial, and
hereafter on application, or by subscription, at the discretion of
the Executive Council, provided there be a sufficient demand for
the same on the part of the alumni.

12

in its judgment the plan is financially feasible.

General Resolution No 8

of the Executive Council be and is hereby approved.

special resolutions.

Special Resolution No. 2 Resolved, That the Convention extends to

Bro. Ernest DeK. Leffingwell {Beta Beta '95) congratulations on the

seas and for its speedy and safe return.

Resolved, That the Recorder of the Convention transmit to Bro.
Leffingwell a copy of this resolution.

hearty thanks of the

hospitality
and entertainment.

(APPENDIX A)

THE COMMUNICATION OF THE EXECUTIVE COUNCIL TO THE
CONVENTION OF 1907

I. Membership. The active membership of the Fraternity on Febru
ary 1, 1907, as reported by the Chapters, was 565, a decrease of 25 since
1906. A table of membership is appended.

II. In Memoriam. Since the last Convention the deaths of the fol
lowing brethen have been reported, and we pay to their memory the
simple but sincere tribute of fraternal regard :
Elisha Taylor, '37, Wendell Lam oroux, '44, Theta, Charles Wilson Opdyke,
'56, Henry Winthrop Gray, '58, Delta, Walter Allen, '63, George Atherton Spalding, '72, Charles Washburn Clark, '75, Frank Sherman Benson,
'76, -Donald McLean Barstow, '89, George Schley Stillman, '01, Beta,
Galusha Aaron Grow, '44, Gamma, Elisha Burr Maynard, '67, Isaac Lea
Nicholson, '69, Zeta, George Franklin Seymour, '50, Philip Woodruff
Holmes, '57, John Krom Rees, '72, Edwin Babcock Holden, '83, Philip
Edwards Johnson, '91, Francis Xavier Snyder, '02, Lambda, Andrew
Peters Wiswell, '73, Kappa, Richard Sutton Rust, '41, William Beinhauer
Silber, '50, Leslie Bingham Cook, '68, Le'verett Marsden Hubbard, '72,
Joel Osmon Sherburn, '73, Calvin Butterfleld Tuttle, '76, Merrill Hitch
cock, '81, Xi, Amory Dwight Mayo, '74, Iota, George Rutledge Gibson,
'74, Phi, Arthur Calvin Redington, '02, Burton Philip Boeheim, '06, Pi,
George Meade Emory, '90, Chi, George Downdall Johnson, '54, William
Henry Benjamin, '57, Beta Beta, Frank Elisha Woodruff, '04, Rho.
III. New Song Book. In its last annual communication the Coun
cil referred the Convention to General Resolution No. Z, of 1905, author
izing the publication of flve hundred copies of the revised song book, pro
vided each Chapter subspribed for eight copies at two dollars each before
June 1, 1905, and reported that as only eleven Chapters had responded no
further steps could be taken without further action by the Convention.
The Convention adopted a resolution authorizing an edition of flve hun
dred copies of the revised song book "as soon as one hundred seventy-flve
(175) copies have been ordered" {General Resolution No. 1, 1906), and a
further resolution that "the delegates be instructed to bring up the mat
ter of the purchase of new song books in their respective Chapters"

{Special Resolution No. 6, 1906). Several of the Chapters sent requests for
copies of the song book, but not enough orders were received to authorize
the publication. The result is that many of the Chapters are nearly des-

14

titute of the Fraternity songs and there are no books for distribution. The
Council would recommend that this Convention authorize the publication
of five hundred copies of the revised song book, to be sold for two dollars
each, and that, in accordance with provision made by the Convention of
1892, Brother Karl P. Harrington, Xi, '82, editor of the last edition, who
has consented to supervise the new edition, be paid a royalty of forty
cents on each song book sold of the new edition.

IV. Discipline op Retired Members. At the Convention of 1906

the Council reported on the question referred by General Resolution No. 8,
of 1905, as to the discipline of Retired Members (Printed Records, 1906,

Appendix D). The Convention adopted a resolution "That Article VI of
Section 8 of the Constitution be amended by striking out the word
'other' {General Resolution I^o. 5, 1906), and also adopted a resolution
providing for the enactment of a By-law by each Chapter to insure due
notice to a member before a vote should be taken on expulsion. {General
Resolution No. 6, 1906). The proposed amendment has not been sub
mitted to the Chapters, owing to delaj' in the printing of the Convention
Records, and will not become operative if objected to by twp or more
Chapters within two weeks in term time after the rtception of the
records. (Constitution, Article X).
V. Fraternity Alumni Associations. In the opinion of the Coun
cil, it would be for the best interests of the Fraternity at large if the
number of our Alumni Associations could be so increased that every
Retired Member would be able at least once ayear to meet with his
brethren in social reunion. Hitherto the Council has had no regular
official intercourse with the Associations existing in various cities ; but it
is believed that if some systematic communication were maintained, the
Alumni would be kept in closer touch with Fraternity affairs, to the
mutual advantage of the Retired and Active Members. If the Convention
approve, the Council would undertake to ascertain the particulars cif
existing Associations, names of officers, times and places of meeting,
number of members, and such other facts as might be deemed useful 

encourage the formation of new Associations wherever practicable fur ;
nish copies of the Convention records, invite suggestions for the o-ood of
the Fraternity, and generally to keep alive and strengthen the Frater
nity Spirit among those who are unable to enjoy the advantao-e of
frequent reunions with Active Members.
VI. Masters of the Rolls. At the Convention held with Beta
Chapter, in 1902, provision was made for the annual appointment of three
Masters of the Rolls, whose duties were prescribed {General Resolution

15

No. 8, 1903). Fro in the annual reports for 1907, it would appear that six of
the Chapters provide lor only two of such officers, one Chapter for only
one, and that flve of the Chapters have omitted to appoint any Masters of
the Rolls for the current year. The importance of the work of these
officers is, perhaps, not fully realized until it becomes necessary to pre

pare for a new catalogue, or to reach the Chapter Members for some
special purpose. But the Council would urge the necessity of maintaining
the Chapter rolls in the best possible condition.

VII. Genehial Fraternity SECRET-iERY: The attention of the Chap
ters has been called by recent communications to the subject of a General

Secretary for the Fraternity, to visit the Chapters, study local conditions
and report to the local Alumni, aud, if necessary, to the general body
through the Executive Council, with a view to advancing the interests of
the Chapters. Copies ot the letter addressed to the Council on this sub
ject by a Committee representing eight Chapters, and of the letter
addressed to the Chapters by a sub-committee, are submitted herewith.
The matter will doubtless be presented to the Convention for considera
tion, and, in view ol its importance, deserves the fullest discussion.
Vllf. Aztec Club. Brother Harry T. Nightingale, Phi, '95, of the
University of Illinois, who expects to attend the approaching Convention,
has asked the privilege of speaking in behalf of the Aztec Club, whose
application for a Charter was denied by the Convention of 1906. The
matter is respectfully referred for your consideration.

IX. Chi Delta Psi, Toronto University. A petition from Chi
Delta Psi Fraternity of Toronto University, Canada, and a letter accom
panying the same, renewing application for a Charter, have been received
to-day, and are herewith submitted.
X. Treasurer's Report. The Report of the Treasurer is presented
herewith
Respectfully submitted,
Herbert L. Bridgman,
George S. Coleman,
George Henry Fox,
George Welling Giddings,
John V. Irwin.

Founders' Fund.
In November, 1898, the Executive Council sent to the Chapters and
to many graduate members of the Fraternity, a circular letter inviting
contributions for the relief of Brother Sterling G. Hadley {Theta '36), of
Waterloo, N. Y., a Founder of the Fraternity, and his invalid wife, who,
through no fault of their own were destitute and in need. In January,
1900, further contributions were solicited. The fund was efficiently ad
ministered by two friends of the family residing at Waterloo, until the
death of Brother Hadley, on September 1, 1901. At that time a balance
remained which with accrued interest became sufficient to procure small
tablets inscribed with the names of the Founders. As it was not practi
cable to return the money to the donors, many of whom did not disclose
their names, it was decided to apply the balance of the fund to the pur
pose indicated. Brother William Ord^ay Partridge {Lambda '85) prepared
a design for the tablet, and the bronze replicas were sent to the Chapters

in June, 1908. A half-tone print of the tablet is inserted herewith
